name: Fall Armyworm
description: An invasive caterpillar pest that feeds on maize and other cereal crops. It causes characteristic window-pane damage on leaves and can devastate young plants.
symptoms: Window-pane damage on young leaves (scraped surface)
Irregular holes and ragged edges on leaves
Frass (caterpillar droppings) visible in leaf whorls
Dead heart in severely infested young plants
Caterpillars with inverted Y-shaped marking on head
treatments: Apply neem-based botanical insecticides early in infestation
Use Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) biopesticide for larvae
Spray emamectin benzoate at 2-3 leaf stage if infestation is severe
Apply chlorantraniliprole as a soil drench for systemic protection
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak pest pressure
Scout fields weekly during vegetative growth
Push-pull strategy with Napier grass as trap crop
Intercrop with legumes to reduce pest establishment
